label: Implementation guidance
title: Design evaluations around the work users need.
context: The speaker contrasts useful work with benchmarks that models can game.
text: The goal here is to try and build evals that are reflective of the actual work people are doing and the work output they want to see, not to build these contrived evals that the models can actually game.

label: Constraint
title: A sandbox does not grant task-scoped authorization.
context: This passage describes the boundary of process isolation. It does not claim that sandboxes are useless.
text: Sandboxes bound what the processes can do, but they don't control what is authorized to act outside the sandbox itself.

label: Reported result
title: Revolut reports a lower invoice for its self-hosted workload.
context: The next segment names Anthropic and OpenAI as the comparison. This is a speaker-reported invoice result, not a total-cost benchmark. Hardware, staffing, and workload equivalence are not established here.
text: In terms of cost, in terms of impact, self-hosting GLM, our blended cost of token is 30 cents per million, and so our invoice is one-tenth of what we were spending on.

label: Implementation guidance
title: Align an evaluator with human judgments before release.
context: The speaker describes the team’s own evaluator checks. Agreement with these examples does not prove correctness on every workload.
text: These data sets, golden truth data sets, we run evals, verify them against the human output, and then try to align to make sure that the judge actually agrees with the human and they're in agreement before we actually ship out a new evaluator.

label: Implementation guidance
title: Include human spend when measuring the cost of a pull request.
context: The next segment completes the point: calculate the real cost per pull request. This is a measurement recommendation.
text: We need to add the AI spend and the human spend, the human salary spend.

label: Constraint
title: Compare token prices only with workload and quality in view.
context: The speaker calls token price a practical proxy. The preceding passage says price per successful task is the goal and is difficult to standardize.
text: Today, price per token is a useful practical proxy, especially for comparable workloads and quality requirements, and gets us closer to delivered output, much closer than the often quoted, all you finance bros out here will have heard this, GPU dollar per hour price, or as we view it, a cost.

label: Future plan
title: Reuse spare capacity for training outside working hours.
context: The preceding passage calls the system an internal prototype. This passage proposes a possible capacity schedule; it does not report a measured saving.
text: Maybe your inference capacity in the day is serving your agents; at night, employees are not using them as much, and you can use that capacity for training instead.

label: Reported result
title: Sonar reports improvements in confidence and reliability.
context: The passage states qualitative results. It does not supply effect sizes or establish that another team would see the same results.
text: We're actually building confidence, and you're seeing results: better security, more confidence in our time to market, improved, or a reduction in number of outages, improved reliability.
